claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered fare (charged $53.58 on a meter), so extra distance driven converts directly into extra fare; the driver's obligation under RD-1 is to take the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause.

The GPS track shows two off-route segments: 22:57–23:03 added 1.14 km (2.63 km driven vs 1.50 km optimal, up to 970 m off route) and 23:21–23:24 added 1.51 km (1.65 km driven vs 0.14 km optimal, up to 985 m off route) — total 2.65 km of unexcused detour.
The whole trip ran 24.9 km against a 21.8 km optimal route (+3.1 km, +14%) and 50.2 min against a 28 min estimate (+21.8 min), confirming the detours were not noise.

No consent exists: the complete, fully timestamped chat record (2 messages, 22:40) contains only a pickup-location message and an ETA message, with nothing from the rider approving any route change before either segment; the rider never agreed to the detour.

The driver's written claim that he 'followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a bare statement contradicted by the GPS records and is not consent — only the rider's own message sent before the segment counts (and no such message exists).

No reasonable-cause exemption applies: there are no traffic incidents recorded near the route during the trip window, and only band-3 (20–29 km/h) speed bands on ECP and Airport Boulevard, which under RD-4(b) serve at most as corroboration and cannot excuse a segment on their own.
